I or T: › [ I or T ] If a train derails or is derailed, it comes off the railway tracks.

T: › [ T ] to prevent a plan or process from succeeding

example: Renewed fighting threatens to derail the peace talks.
重燃的戰火對和談構成了威脅。

NONE: › a type of bicycle gear that works by moving the bicycle chain from one sprocket wheel (= a wheel with a row of tooth-like parts) to another
（腳踏車的）轉鏈輪裝置

example: Set the rear derailleur in the lowest gear, with the chain on the biggest sprocket wheel at the back.
把後輪調到最低擋，就是讓鏈條在後面連到最大的扣鏈齒輪上。

NONE: › completely unable to think clearly or behave in a controlled way, especially because of mental illness
精神錯亂的，發狂的，瘋狂的

example: a deranged criminal/mind/personality
瘋狂的罪犯／混亂的頭腦／狂躁的人格
to be mentally deranged
精神錯亂

C: › a sports event between teams in the same area
（同一地區運動隊伍之間的）體育賽事
› mainly US a sports event in which any competitor can take part

NONE: › a type of horse race
賽馬會

example: a local derby between Manchester United and Manchester City
曼聯隊與曼城隊之間的同城之戰
the annual New Hampshire fishing derby
一年一度的新罕布希爾州釣魚大賽
the Epsom/Kentucky Derby
埃普瑟姆／肯塔基賽馬會

NONE: › to no longer accept that something is true, legal, or important
撤銷對…的承認
› to remove national or local government controls or rules from a business or other activity
對…解禁；撤銷對（貿易等活動）的管制；解除控制

example: The government plans to deregulate the banking industry/the bus system.
政府計劃放寬對銀行業／公共交通系統的管制。

NONE: › Derelict buildings or places are not cared for and are in bad condition.
失修的，破舊的；廢棄的
› a person who has no home or money and often lives outside
無家可歸者，流浪漢

example: a derelict site
廢棄的工地
The theatre has been left to stand/lie derelict.
該劇院一直處於廢棄狀態。

C or U: › [ C or U ] (a) failure to do what you should do

U: › [ U ] (especially of a building) a state of not being cared for

example: What you did was a grave dereliction of duty.
你的所作所為是嚴重瀆職。
The old railway station was in a state of dereliction.
老火車站當時處於廢棄狀態。

NONE: › to laugh at someone or something in a way that shows you think they are stupid or of no value
嘲笑，譏笑

example: He derided my singing as pathetic.
他嘲笑說我的歌聲不堪入耳。
This building, once derided by critics, is now a major tourist attraction.
這座曾被評論家嘲笑的建築如今已成為一個主要的旅遊景點。

NONE: › the situation in which someone or something is laughed at and considered stupid or of no value
嘲笑，嘲諷，嘲弄

example: They treated his suggestion with derision.
他們對他的建議嗤之以鼻。
Her speech was met with hoots/howls of derision.
她的講話遭到一陣陣嘲笑。

NONE: › showing derision
嘲笑的，譏笑的，嘲諷的

example: a derisive comment/remark
嘲諷的評價／話語

NONE: › A derisory amount of money is so small it is silly.
微不足道的，很少的

example: We were awarded a derisory sum.
我們得到的獎金少得可憐。

NONE: › the origin of something, such as a word, from which another form has developed, or the new form itself
起源，出處；衍生物，派生物
› If something is derivative, it is not the result of new ideas, but has been developed from or copies something else.
缺乏獨創性的；模仿的

C: › specialized language a form of something, such as a word, made or developed from another form

› specialized finance & economics a financial product such as an option (= the right to buy or sell something in the future) that has a value based on the value of another product, such as shares or bonds

example: His painting/style is very derivative.
他的油畫／風格有很重的模仿痕跡。

NONE: C1 to get something from something else
從…中得到，從…中獲得

example: The institute derives all its money from foreign investments.
該機構的資金均來自海外投資。
She derives great pleasure/satisfaction from playing the violin.
拉小提琴能給她得到極大樂趣／滿足。

NONE: C1 to come from something
來自於，源自
› a disease in which the skin is red and painful
皮膚炎
› a doctor who studies and treats skin diseases
皮膚科醫生
› the scientific study of the skin and its diseases
皮膚學

C: › an area of the skin supplied by a single spinal nerve
› a tool used to take very thin slices of skin from one part of the body to repair skin in another area

NONE: › the thick layer of skin under the epidermis (= thin outer layer) that contains blood vessels, sweat glands and nerve endings
真皮（位於表皮下方，皮層厚，包括血管、汗腺和神經末梢）

T: › to talk about or treat someone or something in a way that shows you do not respect him, her, or it
› to officially state that a law or rule no longer needs to be obeyed because it no longer has any authority

NONE: › to make something seem less good or important
損害；減損
› to not behave according to the rules of an agreement, acceptable behaviour , etc.
偏離；違背

U: › the act of talking about or treating someone in a way that shows you do not respect him, her, or it
› the act of officially stating that a law or rule no longer needs to be obeyed

NONE: › showing strong disapproval and not showing respect
詆毀的，貶損的，貶低的

example: He made some derogatory comment/remark about her appearance.
他對她的相貌貶低了一番。

NONE: › a type of crane (= a machine with a part like an arm), used for moving things on and off ships
（港口裝卸貨物的）長臂吊車，長臂起重機
› a tower above an oil well that supports the drill (= the machine for making a hole in the ground)
（鑽井）井架，鑽塔
› a person's bottom
臀部
› brave action taken without considering the danger involved
英勇行為；大膽之舉

example: deeds/feats of derring-do
英勇事跡

NONE: › a type of liquid fuel used especially in trucks
柴油
› a member of a Muslim religious group that has an energetic dance as part of its worship
（伊斯蘭教的）托鉢僧

example: The children were spinning around like whirling dervishes.
孩子們像跳舞的托鉢僧一樣旋轉著。
